requirement:
Rust functions, methods, structs, enums, and unions need no annotation or recorded
assessment read merely to account for their existence. A missing annotation or
recorded read produces no warning or validation error solely because the item
exists.

`habeas status` and `habeas author` do not report unreferenced-item counts or
warnings, and do not inspect evidence-file Git history to decide whether source
items have been read.

This does not waive the reference-role obligations of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure`, the annotation requirements for tests
and Cargo examples under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples`, or execution-coverage policy
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Actual assessment reads
remain dependencies checked for freshness under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`.

I checked each clause for an obligation about how the code is built. I looked for a required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface, and found none.

- **"Rust functions, methods, structs, enums, and unions need no annotation or recorded assessment read merely to account for their existence."** This says what must not be demanded. It does not prescribe a module, function, or interface. Any implementation with the same outputs and inputs conforms.
- **The non-waiver paragraph.** It points to `requirements.references.procedure`, `requirements.references.coverage.tests`, `requirements.references.coverage.examples`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions` and `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. These are cited for context, and their own obligations are judged against their own declarations. This paragraph adds no structural obligation of its own.

I did not look for source items that produce this behavior. Finding them would not create a structural obligation, and none is stated.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`. I judged this from the supplied test sources only and did not request any implementation source.

**Obligation 1: ordinary items need no annotation or recorded read, and their absence produces no warning or validation error.**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[ordinary_functions_types_and_test_helpers_require_no_book_connection]` writes a source file with every item kind the text names:
  - a struct, an enum and a union;
  - a free function, an inherent method and a trait method declaration;
  - an unmarked helper inside `mod tests`.
- The file has no references and no evidence. The test asserts that `validate_repository` returns no error mentioning "coverage" or "no {test}". A buggy check that flagged any of these items would fail it.
- The same test asserts that `status_markdown` shows no "Coverage warnings", "has no recent coverage" or "nodes have coverage warnings" text, with `all` both false and true.
- `tests/references.rs#fn[disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file]` shows that an uncited `fn uncited` in scanned files, tracked or untracked, produces no "function uncited" error.
- `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` and `tests/references.rs#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` show the same for functions with `habeas:util` citations and for plain functions.
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_all_files_and_parse_failures]` shows that an uncited `fn uncited` in `src/lib.rs` is not reported. Only the four parse failures are reported.

**Obligation 2: `habeas status` and `habeas author` report no unreferenced-item counts or warnings, and do not inspect evidence-file Git history.**
- `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_retains_repository_findings_without_indexing_unreferenced_functions]` adds an unreferenced `fn unread` and runs `status` with every combination of `--all` and `--verbose`, with and without a selection. It asserts there is no "has no recent coverage" or "coverage warnings" text. It also asserts that real findings (the malformed evidence JSON) are still reported, so the test does not pass merely because output is empty.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics]` adds `ordinary_helper` to the source, initializes Git and runs `author`. It asserts stderr has no "coverage warnings" or "coverage history is incomplete" text. It then commits the evidence, so Git history exists, and runs `status --all` and `author --all`. It asserts the combined output contains no "coverage warnings", "coverage history", "unreferenced" or "ordinary_helper". It also asserts the server subjects stay at 6, so no extra work is done.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference]` is marked for this requirement. It checks that parse errors from Rust discovery fail `author` early, which fits the parse-failure reporting that remains in force.

**Obligation 3: the requirement waives nothing under the cited requirements.** These are `requirements.references.procedure`, `requirements.references.coverage.tests`, `requirements.references.coverage.examples`, the test-coverage requirements and `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. They are context citations and need no test here.
- Tests that confirm the waiver is not over-broad:
  - `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_test_reference_to_an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement]` shows an unreferenced `#[test]` is still reported.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[untracked_examples_are_checked_as_cargo_targets]` shows Cargo examples are still checked.
  - `tests/references.rs#fn[working_directory_references_count_immediately_and_follow_nested_ignore_rules]` shows existing references still produce errors, such as the missing requirement `rules.missing`.

No ambiguity or unacknowledged gap remains.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage
Rust functions, methods, structs, enums, and unions need no annotation or recorded
assessment read merely to account for their existence. A missing annotation or
recorded read produces no warning or validation error solely because the item
exists.
`habeas status` and `habeas author` do not report unreferenced-item counts or
warnings, and do not inspect evidence-file Git history to decide whether source
items have been read.
This does not waive the reference-role obligations of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure`, the annotation requirements for tests
and Cargo examples under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples`, or execution-coverage policy
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Actual assessment reads
remain dependencies checked for freshness under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`.
:::{req} procedure
A source item MUST choose its references under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
for each candidate definition by this procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test designed to verify the definition, it MUST use
`{test}`. A test helper a reviewer reaches by following such a test needs no
reference to the definition.
2. Otherwise, a source root MUST use `{impl}` for a stated structural
obligation. For a non-distributed requirement with test edges, a source
item that only implements tested behavior needs no `{impl}`. For other
definitions, implementation roots continue to use `{impl}`. Code or a type carries out part of a definition when it
makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case
the definition specifies, or when the definition constrains its shape:
fields, variants, serialized form, or validation. A root is such an item
that no other item marked `{impl}` for the definition reaches, where an item
reaches what it calls, the types it uses, and the implementations of trait
methods it calls, and what those reach in turn. An item reached from a root
needs no reference to the definition. An item that is a site of a distributed definition
under {cite}`requirements.references.distributed` needs no reference to it;
its site review covers it.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
Other source items need no reference. In particular, helpers reached from
implementation roots or tests need no individual annotation or assessment read
merely to account for their existence. Reviewers still inspect relevant helpers
when judging tests under {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`.
A `{fixme}` reference is added independently of this procedure.
:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} coverage.examples
Every Cargo example target, each `.rs` file directly under the package's
`examples/` directory, each `examples/<name>/main.rs`, and each `[[example]]`
`path` in `Cargo.toml`, MUST `{cite}` a named example of the book under
{cite}`requirements.examples.definition` in a comment in that file. An example
target without one MUST be a validation error naming the file.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. For display and reference coverage, it MUST derive the inclusive line range
from the first and last bytes of the SDK outline item's attachment-inclusive
span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span`. An empty
span covers the line at its start. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
